44561.why: Built the state and ran it. One line was given parts in every state at once: one ordered from a vendor and still awaiting delivery, one taken from stock with its core showing, and three more still to be picked. Pressing Complete on that line opened the wizard at Pick parts, then Resolve cores, with Receive parts as a further step. After picking and leaving the cores undecided, the line completed anyway - and the ordered part is still sitting at Awaiting Receive, with the cores still showing Ok and Not Ok. So the line completed whatever the state of its parts, which is exactly what this check asks: parts do not block a line from being closed, and nothing about them was changed by completing it.

44562.why: With a tech story required, a line would not complete until it was given one, and an unresolved core was asked for as well.

44563.why: All four routes to Complete are now accounted for. A line's own Complete button completes it, and did so with parts outstanding. The bulk bar's Complete lines completes the selection. Create invoice completes every open approved line as it invoices - seen when a work order went to Invoiced with all six lines closed. And the clock-out window can complete the line, through its Line Completed switch. One caveat worth carrying: that fourth route works through the OLD switch, because the two buttons the design calls for are missing from that window - reported separately against the clock-out check. The route exists; it is not the control the requirement describes.

44565.why: Complete is never greyed out because parts are outstanding, and reopening a finished job item puts it back to Approved with its parts exactly as they were. On the third point the QA lead ruled on 25 September 2026 that the product's behaviour is expected for now, to be revisited: a technician cannot approve, so they never see Complete on a job item themselves; it appears only once an admin has approved the item, and from there the technician may finish it. The wording of this check still reads that a technician cannot finish one, so the check's text and the ruling differ - reported, and the text left exactly as it is.

44566.why: Each status offers what it should. Awaiting approval offers Approve, Decline, Request part and Delete line; approved adds Complete and Authorisation required; declined offers Approve, Authorisation required, Request part and Delete line; finished offers Decline, Authorisation required and Uncomplete. Nothing that belongs to another status is offered, and Complete is not offered before approval.

44567.why: Decline stays on the menu and is greyed out while the job item holds parts that were received or picked, and hovering it gives the reason in the words the check asks for: the line cannot be declined while it holds received or picked parts, move the parts to another line or return them.

44568.why: With parts seeded into each state: a quoted part offers nothing, one authorised to order offers Order, one in stock offers Pick, one awaiting arrival offers Receive, and a received part offers nothing. A core part follows its parent and is never offered a choice of its own.

44569.why: With receiving required, Receive sits on the part row; with it off, Receive moves into the part's three-dot menu and is never removed outright.

44570.why: Built a line whose part had not arrived - ordered but still waiting - and declined it. The line went to Declined and the part went straight back to Quoted, which is what this check asks. The other half of it, that parts which HAVE arrived keep their state, turns out to be protected by the product rather than tested: Decline is greyed out on every line holding received or picked parts, with the reason spelled out on hover. So the situation where a decline could strip an arrived part cannot be reached at all - which is a stronger guarantee than the one the check describes, and was confirmed on four separate lines whose Decline was greyed for exactly that reason.

44591.why:
Re-judged against the corrected check. The QA lead ruled on 28 September 2026 that a supplier invoice number is unique and is not reusable, and the check has been rewritten to say so. What was seen on the shop matches that ruling exactly, so the product is right and the earlier failure was the check being wrong, not the build.

What was seen: the first order accepted a fresh invoice number and received its parts. A second order for the same supplier, given the same number, was refused with "Invoice 'ZZAUTOTEST-SHARED-2' is already in use" and received nothing. Tried twice on two different pairs of orders.

The rest of the check also holds: a person who may only look at suppliers and orders reads the whole list but is offered no way to receive, while a manager on the same page gets a Receive on every row; no selling price appears anywhere on the receive page or in the receiving window; and with the money permission off the cost and total columns are gone rather than blanked, with receiving still working.

44592.why: Run as a person carrying the receive-later permission, which had to be granted first - and the granting is itself the finding. The administrator account does NOT carry it, and for that account Receive is a plain button with no caret at all. Grant the permission and the same control grows a caret: the part row then reads Awaiting, Receive and a drop-down arrow. So the split button is genuinely gated by the permission, which is what this check is really asking. Used end to end: in the receive window each vendor group carries its own Receive Later button beside Receive Parts with its count, both greyed until something is ticked. Ticking a single part made Receive Later pressable on its own, and pressing it moved only that part - its row now reads Receive Later while the other three still read Awaiting Receive with their drop-down. So the choice is made per part, not for the whole work order. Worth noting for whoever reads this next: a role named ZZAUTOTEST Receive Later already existed, and its receive-later switch was OFF. The name was not evidence. It was switched on, saved and read back before anything was measured.

44593.why: Without the permission, Receive is a plain button with no caret anywhere, and with receiving not required there is no split button at all.

44594.why: Create invoice opened the wizard on a work order with a part still to receive, and the wizard named exactly what was outstanding.

44596.why: Watched across several full runs of the completion wizard. Every step carries its OWN action and there is no general Continue button anywhere: the picking step offers Pick All, the cores step offers Save Core Decisions alongside Continue Without Resolving, and the receiving step offers Receive Parts. Pressing a step's own action both does the work and moves the wizard on - after Pick All the wizard went straight to the cores step with picking shown as done, and after the cores were decided it moved on again. The receiving step opens the same window used elsewhere, grouped by vendor, each group carrying its own invoice number, invoice date and delivery note, the parts with a tick box each, and Receive Parts with a count beside Receive Later - so the per-part defer is offered there too. One thing to be straight about: the steps were driven forward, not closed and reopened mid-run, so whether a half-finished run remembers where it was is not covered here.

44597.why:
All three runs now done, and each one ends somewhere different - which is the whole point of this check.

Started from a line: the questions are asked, the line closes, and you are put back on the job's own list of lines. No bill, nothing else opened.

Started from "Complete All Lines": with two lines still open and every one of them selected, the bar names itself "Complete All Lines" rather than the single-line wording. The run asked about the four old units that could be settled, then about the one part still waiting to arrive, and finished with "Complete Lines (2)". Both open lines closed, the old units now read as returned, and the job stayed exactly where it was - no bill, no payment screen. The sign-off action then appeared in the header, where before there had been nothing at all. It is offered but not yet usable, because one part on the job is still waiting to be received and the shop is set to require that before work is signed off - which is a separate rule doing its job, not this one failing.

Started from raising the bill: it ends on the payment screen with the job billed and its open lines closed.

Set-up note for whoever runs this by hand: this needs a job with two or more lines still open. A line that is already finished can be put back by opening its three-dot menu and choosing "Uncomplete", which returns it to the approved state ready to be completed again.

44599.why: My earlier failure is withdrawn. The QA lead pointed out that what the requirement calls Send is the product's Send to Portal, and I have now seen it myself: on a work order marked Estimate with a line awaiting approval, the header carries New Line, the three-dot menu, and an icon button whose label and tooltip both read Send to Portal, enabled. On an invoiced work order the same button is present and greyed out, which matches what he described - it becomes active only while a line is awaiting approval. I missed it because I read buttons by their text, and an icon button has no text: it reported itself as how_to_reg, the icon's own name, which I had actually captured and logged without recognising it. Everything else this check asks for was already right: Create invoice sits in the three-dot menu while a line is still open, is promoted to a button beside New Line once every line is complete, and is shown greyed out with its reason where a line still awaits approval. One observation worth recording rather than raising: Send to Portal is not rendered on every work order - it was absent from several I sampled - so which states show it greyed versus not at all is not yet mapped.

44600.why: Carried out end to end rather than avoided. Pressing Create invoice on a work order with outstanding work opened the wizard at its cores step; once each core was decided, Create Invoice became pressable, the invoice was created, every open approved line went to Complete, the work order now reads Invoiced, and the New Customer Payment screen opened - which is what this check asks for. I had recorded this as impossible because it would create a real invoice; on a branch whose data the QA lead has said is not real, that was a restriction I placed on myself. Not covered: the case also asks for the case where a deposit already covers the whole amount and the payment screen is skipped. No work order here carries such a deposit, so that one point is untested and is named here rather than glossed over.

44601.why:
All five parts of this check now hold, the last two having needed people built specially for them.

Settled earlier: a job whose only line is declined offers no way to finish it; once a bill exists neither finishing action is offered anywhere, not in the header and not behind its three dots; and somebody who may not see money is offered no way to raise a bill at all.

Settled now, on one and the same job so the comparison is fair:
- A person allowed to sign work off but not to bill for it is offered "Mark Reviewed", and it works for them. On a job that is ready to be billed instead, their header offers nothing at all - no billing action in the header and none behind the three dots. That is exactly "sign it off, then nothing further".
- A person allowed neither to sign off nor to bill is offered nothing they can use: the sign-off button is greyed out and will not press, and there is no billing action anywhere.
- A manager holding both sees the same sign-off button live on the same job, which is what proves the greyed-out one is the permission working and not a button that is broken for everybody.

One difference worth telling you about, which is NOT a fault in the product: the written check says a person who may only finish work "sees nothing in the header". What they actually see is the sign-off button greyed out. They cannot use it, so the protection is real; and the product's own written rule elsewhere is that a blocked action is shown greyed with its reason rather than hidden. The source says nothing either way about this particular case, so nothing was invented - this is flagged for you to settle rather than raised as a fault.

44602.why: The parts menu holds Move, Return, the fee or discount item, and Receive part only when receiving is optional. The job item's own menu holds Request part, Add line note, Save as canned line, Edit labor, Receive parts with a count, Authorisation required, and Uncomplete on a finished item. On a work order that has been invoiced or paid, Uncomplete is not offered at all, which is the block this check asks for.

44603.why: Request part is not offered on a finished job item. Uncomplete appears only on a finished one and disappears the moment it is reopened. For a person without permission to order parts, Receive part is not in any menu on the page.

44604.why: Move up moved the part above the one before it within its line, its core followed it, and the new order was still there after the page was reloaded.

44605.why:
All three parts of this check now have an answer.

Moving a part to another line works. Open the part's own menu on the line, choose Move, pick the line to move it to, then press the button twice: it first reads "Move To Line" and then changes to "Please Confirm", and the part only moves on that second press. A part sitting on a finished line moves just the same.

On a work order that has already been invoiced, the parts cannot be put in a different order at all. There is no drag handle on any part row and no part menu to open, and when the request is made directly the shop system turns it down and says so: "Parts can no longer be reordered on this work order (status: Invoiced)." This is what the check expects to happen.

To be sure that refusal was the product and not a fault in the way it was measured, the same reordering was done first on a work order that is still open, through the screen: it went through and the parts visibly changed places.

Two people reordering the same line at the same moment: the second one to save wins, quietly. Nobody is warned that they have just overwritten somebody else's ordering. The shop system only objects when parts have been added or taken off the line in the meantime, and then it says "The parts submitted for reordering no longer match this line. Please refresh and try again." Nothing written down says what should happen when two people simply reorder at once, so this is recorded as something to put to the Product Owner rather than treated as a fault.

44606.why: Receive later is in the Work orders section of a role as a single yes-or-no switch, not a create-and-edit row, and it is off in all eight roles that were read. It is the only new permission in the list.

44607.why:
Every action this check covers is now tied to its own permission, tested with somebody who has it and somebody who does not.

Settled earlier: picking follows the picking permission, ordering follows the ordering permission, and money follows the money permission - with money off, every money column disappears from the job, the orders page and the receiving page.

Settled now:
- Signing a job off follows the sign-off permission: live for somebody who holds it, greyed out for somebody who does not, on the same job.
- Raising the bill follows the billing permission: a person without it is offered no billing action at all on a job that is ready for one.
- The supplier and order pages follow the supplier permission: a look-only person reads the whole orders list but is given no tick boxes, no Receive on any row and nothing for a selection, while a manager on the same page gets a Receive on every row. The bulk version is gated by the same permission as the single one - it does not appear separately.
- Creating parts follows the catalogue permission: with look-only catalogue rights the parts area opens and every tab is there, but no way to create a part is offered.
- The settings pages follow the application settings permission: with it taken away, going to the settings address does not open a stripped-down page, it sends the person back to their job list.

The finding recorded earlier still stands and is worth repeating: these permissions are NOT one-for-one. Switching the money permission off also switches off part sales, billing, ordering and the supplier ledger - the product warns about it and will not let them be separated. So a person who may order parts but may not see money cannot be built at all, and any future check that assumes that pairing is asking for something the product refuses to create.

44608.why: With financial access removed, the work order's Rate, Margin and Total columns are gone from the page entirely and not one money amount is drawn. The work columns - Status and Action - stay. The fields are removed, not masked.

44609.why: A person without a permission does not see the action at all: Pick, Order and Receive were absent from the bar and the rows rather than shown and refused. No money value reached the screen either.
